Elnathan’s overlapping marriage dates

Research in progress

FamilySearch gives the Jane Hayes marriage as 1751 and Jane’s death as July 16, 1761. Its expanded family group also gives April 20, 1759 in Fairfield for Lucine Griffin (1732–1803), with Rebecca (1763–1794), Naomi (1765–1844), Abigail (1768–1849), James (1770–1838), and Joseph (1774–1844). The 1759 date overlaps Jane’s lifetime. The archive retains the five existing paternal links but does not assign Lucine as their mother or publish this marriage as established. His earlier 1777 birth label has been corrected; the overlapping marriage chronology remains unresolved.

Lambson

Trace the reported Calvin Coolidge connection

Research in progress

FamousKin lists Barnabas Lambson as Calvin Coolidge’s seventh-great-grandfather. The reported chain is Barnabas → Martha Lambson → Martha Rice → John Bent → Martha Bent → Eliab Brewer → Israel Chase Brewer → Sarah Almeda Brewer → John Calvin Coolidge → President Calvin Coolidge. The archive’s recorded line proceeds through Martha’s brother Joseph. The Coolidge Foundation lists the chart as an outside resource, with an explicit accuracy disclaimer. This is a reported collateral connection, not a completed genealogical proof; no exact cousin degree is assigned.

Next evidence to locate Check each parent–child link in the Coolidge descent using cited vital, church, probate and published genealogical records; compare the common Barnabas identity and the archive’s Joseph line. Preserve conflicting dates and surname variants rather than merging on names alone.

People Barnabas Lamson / Lambson, Martha Lamson Rice, Joseph Lambson, Norma Lucille Lambson

Lambson

Identify Glenn’s cavalry service and resolve the repeated dates

Probable

The 1924 Utah military roster lists a starred Glenn C. Lambson of Springville under cavalry. Its key identifies the star as overseas duty. This is a probable match to Glenn Cody Lambson, born in Springville in 1898, and supports the family’s overseas-service recollection without independently establishing France. Both enlistment and discharge are printed as May 9, 1918. No corrected discharge year, regiment, or exact deployment location is assigned.

Next evidence to locate Locate a full-name service card, enlistment or discharge document, and passenger or transport record. Compare birth details or a service number to establish identity, resolve the dates, and test Clara’s recollection of France.
